23.9: If any man have wrath against his companion, let him be reconciled.
23.10: If any man have’ a conscience without faith, let him confess [it].
23.11: If any man have a thought foreign to the commandments, let him depart.
23.12: If any man have fallen into sin, let him not hide himself: he may not hide himself.
23.13: If any man have a disordered reason, let him not draw near.
23.14: If any man be defiled, if any man is not firm, let him give place.
23.15: If any man be a stranger to the commandments of Jesus, let him depart.
23.16: If any man despise the prophets, let him separate himself: from the wrath of the Only-begotten let him deliver himself.
23.17: Let us not despise the cross.
23.19: We have our Lord as onlooker, the Father of Lights with the Son, [and] the angels who visit [us].
23.21: [Lift] up your hearts to offer for the salvation of life and of holiness.
23.22: In the wisdom of God let us receive the grace which has been bestowed upon us.
23.23: Then let the bishop say, giving and rendering thanks with an awed voice: Our Lord [be] with you. And let the people say: And with your spirit.
23.24: Let the bishop say: [Lift] up your hearts. Let the people say: They are [lifted up] to the Lord. Let the bishop say: Let us give thanks to the Lord.
23.25: And let all the people say: It is fitting and right.
23.26: And let the bishop cry: Holy things in holy [persons].
23.27: And let the people call out: In heaven and on earth without ceasing.
23.28: Let the bishop immediately say: We render thanks to You, O God, the Holy One, Con- firmer of our souls, and Giver of our life, the Treasure of incorruptibility, and Father of the Only-begotten, our Savior, whom ‘in the latter times you did send to us as a Savior and Proclaimer of Your purpose For it is Your purpose that we should be saved in You.
23.29: Our heart gives thanks to You, O Lord, [our] mind, [our] soul, with all [its] thinking, that Your grace may come upon us, O Lord, so that we may continually praise You, and Your Only-begotten Son, and Your Holy Spirit, now and alway, and for ever and ever. Amen.
23.30: O You Power of the Father, the Grace of the nations, Knowledge, true Wisdom, the Exaltation of the meek, the Medicine of souls, the Confidence of us who believe, for You are the Strength of the righteous, the Hope of the persecuted, the Haven of those who are buffeted, the Illuminator of the perfect, the Son of the living God’ make to arise on us, out of Your gift which cannot be searched into, courage, might, reliance, wisdom, strength, unlapsing faith, unshaken hope, the knowledge of Your Spirit, meekness [and] uprightness, so that alway, O Lord, we Your servants, and all the people, may praise You purely, may bless You, may give thanks to You, Lord, at all times, and may beg You.
23.31: And also let the bishop say.
23.32: You, Lord, the Founder of the heights, and King of the treasuries of light, Visitor of the heavenly Sion, King of the orders of archangels,’ of Dominions, Praises, Thrones, Raiments, Lights, Joys, Delights, the Father of kings, who hold all in Your hand, and supply’” [all] by Your reason, through Your Only-begotten Son who was crucified for our sins: You, Lord, sent Your Word, who is of Your counsel and covenants by whom you made all things, being well pleased with Him, into a virgin womb; who, when He was conceived,
23.33: [and] made flesh, was shown to be Your Son, being born of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin’; who, fulfilling Your; will, and preparing a holy people,” stretched forth His hands to suffering, that He might loose from sufferings and corruption and death those who have hoped in you; who when He was betrayed to voluntary suffering that He might raise up those who had slipped, and find those who were lost, and give life to the dead, and loose [the pains of] death, and rend the bonds of the Devil, and fulfill the counsel of the Father, and tread down Sheol, and open the way of life, and guide the righteous to light, and fix the boundary, and lighten the darkness, and nurture the babes, and reveal the resurrection; taking bread, gave it to His disciples, saying, Take, eat, this is My Body which is broken for you for the forgiveness of sins.
23.34: When you shall do’ this, you make’ My resurrection. Also the cup of wine which He mixed He gave for a type of the Blood which he shed for us.
23.36: Remembering therefore Your death and resurrection, we offer to You bread and the cup, giving thanks to You who alone are God for ever, and our Savior, since You have promised to us to stand before You and to serve You in priesthood. Therefore we render thanks to You, we Your servants, O Lord.
23.37: And let the people say likewise.
23.38: And also let [the bishop] say: We offer to You this thanksgiving, Eternal Trinity, O
23.39: Lord Jesus Christ, O Lord the Father before! Whom all creation and every nature trembles fleeing into itself, O Lord the Holy Spirit; we have brought this drink and this food of Your Holiness [to You]; Cause that it may be to us not for condemnation, not for reproach, not for destruction, but for the medicine and support of our spirit.
23.40: Yes, O God, grant us that by Your Name every thought of things displeasing to You may flee away.
23.41: Grant, O God, that every proud conception may be driven away from us by Your Name which is written within the veils of Your sanctuaries, those high ones—a Name which, when Sheol hears [it], it is amazed, the depth is torn, the spirits are driven away, the dragon is bruised,’ unbelief is cast out, disobedience is subdued, anger is appeased, envy does not work, pride is reproved, avarice rooted out, boasting taken away, arrogance humbled, [and] every root of bitterness destroyed.
23.42: Grant therefore, O Lord, to our innermost eyes to see You, praising You and glorifying You, commemorating’ You [and] serving You, having a portion in You alone, O Son and Word of God, who subdue all things. Sustain to the end those who have gifts of revelations Confirm those who have a gift of healing! Make those courageous who have the power of tongues." Keep those who have the word of doctrine upright.
23.43: Care for those who do Your will alway. Visit the widows. Help the orphans. Remember those who have fallen asleep in the faith. And grant us an inheritance with
23.44: Your saints, and bestow [upon us] the power to please You as they also pleased You.
23.45: Feed the people in uprightness: sanctify us all, O God; but grant that all those who partake and receive of Your Holy Things may be made one with You, so that they may be filled with the Holy Spirit, for the confirmation of the faith in truth, that they may lift up always a doxology to You, and to Your beloved Son Jesus Christ, by whom praise and might [be] to You, with Your Holy Spirit for ever and ever.
23.47: The deacon: Karnestly let us beg our Lord and our God that He may bestow upon us concord of spirit.
23.48: The bishop: Give us concord in the Holy Spirit, and heal our souls by this offering, that we may live in You in all the ages of ages.
23.50: Let the people also pray in the same [words].
23.51: After these things the seal of thanksgiving thus: Let the Name of the Lord be blessed for ever.
23.53: The priest: Blessed is He that has come in the Name of the Lord. Blessed [is] the Name of His praise.
23.54: And let all the people say: So be it, so be it.
23.55: Let the bishop say: Send the grace of the Spirit upon us.
23.56: If the bishop be polluted, let him not offer, but let a presbyter offer. Also let him not receive of the mystery, not as though he were defiled, but because of the honor of the altar. But after he has fasted and bathed in pure water, let him approach and minister. Similarly also a presbyter. And if also a widow be menstruous, let her not approach.
23.57: Similarly if a woman or a layman or any of the company [of the clergy be polluted], let him not approach, for the honor [of the altar] except after fasting and bathing.
23.58: Let the priests first receive, thus: the bishops, presbyters, deacons, widows, readers, subdeacons. After these those that have gifts, those newly baptized, babes. The people thus: old men, virgins and the rest. The women [thus]: deaconesses, and after that the rest.
23.59: Let each one when he receives the thanksgiving" say before he partakes: Amen. After that let him pray thus; after that he receives the Eucharist let him say: Holy, Holy, Holy, Trinity ineffable, grant me to receive to life’ this Body, [and] not to condemnation.
23.60: And grant me to bring forth the fruits that are pleasing to You, so that when I shall be shown to be pleasing to You I may live in You, doing Your commandments; and [that] with boldness I may call You Father, when I call for Your kingdom and Your will [to come] to me.” -May Your Name be hallowed! In me, O Lord; for You are mighty and [to be] praised, and to You be praise for ever and ever.
23.62: After the prayer let him receive.
23.63: When he takes of the Cup, let him say twice Amen,’ for a complete symbol of the Body and Blood.
23.64: After all receive, let them pray, giving and rendering thanks for the reception, the deacon saying.
23.65: Let us give thanks to the Lord, receiving His Holy Things, so that the reception [of them] may be for the life and salvation of our souls. Let us beg and beg [His grace], raising a doxology to the Lord our God.
23.67: O Lord, Giver of light eternal,’ the Helmsman of souls, the Guide of saints; Give us understanding eyes which always look to You, and ears which hear You only, so that our soul may be filled with grace. Create in us a clean heart,’ O God; so that we may alway comprehend Your greatness.
23.68: O God, Wonderful, who love man,’ make our souls better, and, by this Eucharist which we, Your servants, who fail in much, have [now] received, form our thoughts so that they shall not swerve: for Your kingdom is blessed, O Lord God, [who are] glorified and praised in Father and in Son and in Holy Spirit, both before the worlds, and now, and alway, and for the ages and for ever and ever without end.

24.1: [Lf the priest consecrate oil for the healing of those who] suffer, let him say thus, quietly placing the vessel before the altar.
24.2: O Lord God, who have bestowed upon us the Spirit, the Paraclete the Lord, the saving and unshaken Name, which is hidden from the foolish but revealed to the wise; O Christ, who sanctified us, and by Your mercies do make the servants whom you choose wise with the wisdom that is Yours, who sent the knowledge of Your Spirit to us sinners by the holiness which is Yours, bestowing on us the power of the Spirit; who are the Healer of every sickness and of every suffering; who gave the gift of healing to those who were counted worthy of this by You; send on this oil, which is the type of Your fatness, the delivering [power] of Your good compassion, that it may deliver those who labour and heal those who are sick, and sanctify those who return, when they approach to Your faith; for You are mighty and [to be] praised for ever and ever.

25.1: Likewise, the same also over water.

26.1: At early dawn let the bishop assemble the people, so that the service may be finished before the rising of the sun.
26.2: When he says the First Hymn of Praise, of the Dawn, the presbyters and deacons and the rest, the faithful also, [standing] close by, let him say thus.
26.4: And let the people say: It is fitting and right.
26: HYMN OF PRAISE FOR THE DAWN
HYMN OF PRAISE OF THE SEAL
26.5: The bishop: It is fitting and right that we should praise and laud and give thanks to You, who made all, ineffable God.
26.6: Stretching forth! Our souls upward, we raise to You, O Lord, a hymn of praise for the morning,—to You who are all-wise, powerful, great in mercies, O God, the Confirmer and Raiser-up of our souls; we praise You, the Word who before the worlds were begotten of the Father, and rest alone with Your saints who are praised with the hymns of the archangels——You the Maker, who were not made with hands, and who make known holy things which are invisible, pure, and spotless——You who have made known to us the hidden mysteries of wisdom, and promised to us immortal light; we lift up praise to You in pure holiness, we Your servants, O Lord.
26.7: And let the people say: We praise You, we bless You, we give thanks to You, O Lord; and we beg you, O our God.
26.8: Also [let] the bishop say: O God, the Begetter of light, the Principle of life, the Giver of knowledge, the Gift of grace, the Maker of souls, who make things [that are] beautiful, the Giver of the Holy Spirit, the Treasure of Wisdom, and the Maker of good things, the Lord, the Teacher of holiness, who rule the worlds by Your will, the Receiver of pure prayers; we praise You, the Only-begotten Son, the First-born and Word of the Father, who bestowed all Your grace on us who call upon You, the Helper, and upon the Father who begat You; who have an essence that cannot be injured, where neither moth nor worm! Does corrupt; who give to all that with all their heart trust in You those things which the angels have desired to behold; who are the Guardian of light eternal and [of] treasures incorruptible; who have by the will of Your Father shed light on the darkness which [is] in us; who from the depth have raised us up to light; who have given us life out of death, and bestowed upon us freedom out of slavery; who by the cross have made us of the household of Your Father, and by Your gospel have guided us to the heights of heaven, and have comforted us by Your prophets; who in Your own Person have made us of the household of God the Father of lights; grant us, O Lord, that we may praise You, our God, so that always with unceasing thanksgiving’ we may speak praises to You, we Your servants, O Lord.
26.9: The people: We praise You, we bless You, we give thanks to You, we beg you, O our God.
26.10: Let the bishop also say: We sing to You with our mouths this triple hymn of praise as a figure of Your kingdom, O Son of God, who [are] by eternity; who [are] above all, with the Father; whom all creation praises, trembling with fear of Your Spirit; at whom all nature trembles in fear and [whom] every soul of the righteous blesses; with whom all we have taken refuge; who have made confusion, storms, [and] wind to cease from us; who have been to us an haven of rest, and a place to flee to from corruption; in whom we have hope of eternal salvation; who make the peacefulness of fine weather for those who are buffeted on the seas and with the tempests; who in sicknesses are
26.11: Entreated and heal without price; who are with those that are shut up in prison; who have loosed us from the bonds of death; [who are] the Comforter of the poor, and of those who mourn, and of those who have laboured and wearied themselves with the cross; who turn away from us every menace!; who for us have reproved the craft of Satan; who drive away his menaces, and give us courage; who thrust away all error from those that trust in You; whom the prophets and apostles praised secretly: we praise You, O Lord, we lift up to You a doxology, so that, having known You, we may rest in the habitations of life, doing Your will alway.
26.12: And grant to us, O Lord, to walk according to Your commandments, and in mercy visit us all, both small and great, the prince and his people, the shepherd and his flock; for You, O Lord, are our God, and blessed and praised [is] Your kingdom—the kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, both before the worlds, and now and always, and for the ages, and for ever and ever without end.
26.13: And let the people say: Amen.
26.14: Let them sing psalms and four hymns of praise; one by Moses, and of Solomon, and of the other prophets. Thus: little singing-boys; two virgins; three deacons; three presbyters. And so let the hymn of praise be said by the bishop, or by one of the presbyters.
26.15: Let wt be said thus: The grace of our Lord [be] with you all. And let the people say: And with your spirit.
26.16: And let the priest say: Also let us praise our Lord.
26.17: And let the people say: Meetly and rightly. Let the priest say: Let your hearts be fixed. And let the people say: We have [them fixed] with the Lord.
26.18: O Lord, the Father, the Giver of light, the Author of all power and of all spirits, the Sealer of eternal light, and the Guide of life, the Maker of felicity and immortality, who have made us to pass through material darkness, and have bestowed upon us immaterial light; who have loosed the bonds of disobedience and crowned us with the faith which is Yours; who do not keep far off from Your servants, but are in them always; who do not neglect those [souls] which with labour and in Your fear beg You; who know all things before they are thought, and search out all things before they are considered, and give what You will give before we ask You; who are well pleased to hear’ those who with heart undoubting serve You, O King of the highest lights and the soldiery of heaven, who hear the archangels when they praise You, and are pleased in them; Answer us, O Lord, we beg you.
26.19: Grant us with boldness [with] unceasing voice to praise You, to laud You, to lift up to You a doxology; so that being guarded by You and guided in light, we Your servants, O Lord, may constantly praise You.
26.20: The people: We praise You, we bless You, we give thanks to You, O Lord; and we beg you, O our God.
26.21: The priest: O Lord Jesus, hear us, O Holy One, who were the Voice of the dumb and the irrational, the Strength of the paralysed, the Giver of light to the blind, the Guide of the lame, the Cleanser of the lepers, the Curer of material fluxes, the Healer of the deaf and dumb, the Reprover of death, the Tormentor of darkness, the Ray of light, and the Lamp that is not quenched, the Sun that is not darkened [and] rests [not]; but who always give light to Your saints; who have established all things together for the good likeness of comeliness; who are the well-tempered Reason; who have plainly given light to all; who are the Savior of the sons of men, and the Converter of souls; who are the Provider of all things as is right, the Maker of the angels, who adorn all; the Thought of the Father; who found the worlds in prudence and wisdom, and establish them together; and were sent from Your eternal Father to us; the Intelligence of the Spirit who may not be apprehended or understood, the Maker-known of things invisible; You are glorious, and Your Name is Wonderful.’ Therefore we also, Your servants, O Lord, give praise to You.
26.22: The people: We praise You, we bless You, we give thanks to You, O Lord; we beg you, O our Lord.
26.23: The priest: We sing, O holy Lord, this threefold hymn of praise to You, who gave us a faith in You which cannot be loosed, by which you did make us to conquer the bonds of death; who created upright minds in them that trust in You, that they might be gods; who by the Spirit gave to us to tread under foot all the power of the enemy that we! May not profane those things which may not be profaned; who by Your mediation have made friendship for us with Your Father.
26.24: Answer us Your servants, O Lord, [You] whom without ceasing! We entreat, who at our supplication give [us] power against the adversary; whom alway we ask, as [it were], for the overthrow of the Evil one; Hear us, O King Eternal; comfort the widows, help the orphans; pity and cleanse those who are possessed with unclean spirits, give wisdom to the unwise; convert those who go astray; deliver those who are in prison; guard us all, for You, O Lord, are our God; blessed and glorious is Your kingdom.

27.1: After this let the prayer be completed, and let the reader then read the Prophets and the rest; let the presbyter or deacon read the Gospel; and then let the bishop or presbyter teach those things which are convenient and profitable. After that let there be a prayer, and let the catechumens receive a laying on of the hand.

28.1: After that let the bishop teach the mysteries to the people. But if he is not present, let a presbyter speak so that the faithful may know to whom they are approaching and who is their’ God and Father. Then let the teaching of the mysteries be said thus.
28.2: [MYSTAGOGIA oR] INITIATION INTO THE MYSTERIES WHICH IS SAID BEFORE THE OFFERING TO THE FAITHFUL [We confess] Him who is pre-existent, and was present,
28.3: As we believe, we confess Him who is our Light, Salvation, Savior, Protector, Helper, Teacher, Deliverer, Rewarder, Assister, Strength, Wall; our Shepherd, Entrance, Door, Way,
28.4: Life, Medicine, Provision, Drink, [and] Judge. We confess Him passible [yet] not passible, Son?
28.5: [yet] not created,’ dead [yet] alive, the Son of the Father, incomprehensible [yet] comprehensible; who, [Himself] sinless, has borne our sins when He left the Father’s heaven; whose Body being broken becomes our salvation, and [His] Blood and Spirit [our] life and holiness, and the water our cleansing; who gives light to the hearts of those who fear Him, being with them in all things; who has made us strangers to the whole way of the Devil; the Renewer of souls, in whom we all have put our trust.
28.6: He, being God, and before the worlds with the Father, eternal God, when He saw the world perishing in the bonds of sin, and trodden down by the power of a crafty wild beast, and made subject to death through ignorance and error, determining to heal the race of mankind, came to a virgin womb, though hidden from all the camps of the heavenly ones, and cast into ignorance [the] opposing hosts.
28.7: But when [He], the Incorruptible, clothed Himself with corruptible flesh, making flesh which was under death to be incorruptible, He thus showed in the flesh of dead Adam, with which He clothed Himself, an example’ of incorruptibility, by which example the things of corruption were abolished.
28.8: He, then, having become Man, the Son of God, the Lord, who took [on Him] the dead race of Adam in all its kinds, by emptying [Himself!], He who is the First, came to birth, as Man, though He is God; He who was foreknown by the prophets,” and preached by the apostles, and lauded by angels, and glorified by the Father of all’ He was crucified for us; and His cross is our life, our strength, [our] salvation, for it is the hidden mystery,‘ the ineffable joy, and through it the whole nature of mankind, always bearing it, is made inseparable from God, for it is the virtue benign’ and inseparable & from God, that cannot be spoken as is fitting by these lips, [and] that was hidden from the beginning; but now the mystery which is revealed, which is for the faithful, shall be, not as it seems to be, but as it is.
28.9: This cross in which we boast, so that we may be glorified, [and] the bearers of which, the faithful and perfect, separate their souls from everything that can be felt, from everything that is seen, as from a thing which is not true? —by this ask for yourselves, O you who quit you like men’; make deaf your visible ears"; make blind your bodily eyes; so that you may know the will of Christ and all the mystery of your salvation.
28.10: Holy men and women, whose property it is to make your boast in the Lord, listen to the inward man.
28.11: Our Lord, when He taught us and appointed to us a covenant, and made us of [His] household, and came, after His passion, into Sheol, made captive all the earth—He who made the nature of death captive to life, and Death when it saw Him descending in His soul’ to Sheol, was deceived, and hoped that He was food for him, as was his custom.
28.12: But when he saw in Him the beauty of the Godhead, he cried out with [his] voice, saying: Who is this that has clothed Himself with Man who [was] under me, and has conquered me? Who is this that snatches from destruction flesh which was bound by me? Who is this! That has clothed Himself with earth but [Himself] is heaven?
28.13: Who is this that was born in corruptibility, but suffers no corruption Who is this [that is] a stranger to my laws? Who is this that makes captive those that are mine? Who is this that strives with the power of burning Death, and conquers darkness? What is this new glory which [is] in this vision that prevents me from doing the things which I would? Who is this new dead One without sin?
28.14: Who is this that by the abundance of light extinguishes darkness, and does not allow me to have rule over those that are mine, but draws to heaven the souls which were given to me? What is this glory which prevents the body from being corruptible? Who is this whom I cannot touch? What is this glory unsearchable to its surroundings? Woe’ is me!
28.15: I am put to flight’ by Him and by those things which are His, for I cannot injure them.
28.16: He, being the Christ, who was crucified, by whom the [things] that were on the left hand were’ [placed] on the right hand, and those which were beneath [were] as those which [were] above, and those which [were] behind as those which [were] before, when He rose from the dead, and trod down Sheol, and by death killed Death"; after He rose on the third day He gave thanks to the Father, saying: I give thanks to You, O My Father, not with these lips which are fixed together, nor yet with a corporeal tongue through which truth and lying go out, nor with this created and material word; but I give thanks to You, the King, with that Voice which through You understands all [things], which comes not by a bodily organ, which falls not on carnal ears, which
28.17: Is not in the world and is not left on earth, but with this Voice, the Spirit who! Is in Us, only speaking to You, O Father, loving You, praising You, through whom also the whole choir of perfect saints calls You beloved, [calls] You Father, [calls] You Sustainer, [calls] You Helper; for You are all, and all [are] in You; for whatever is, is Your and not another’s, but is Your alone, who are for ever and ever.
28.19: Let the shepherd know the mysteries of all nature. After I have prayed to the Father, as you know and see, I am taken up, says Jesus.
28.20: Therefore it is right that the shepherd should speak the teaching of the Initiation into the mysteries, so that they may know of whom in the holy things they are partaking, and what memorial they are making’ through the Eucharist.
28.21: And at the end, after this, let him say thus: As then we also have taken refuge in Him, and have learnt that it is in Him alone to give, let us beg from Him those things which He said that He would give us, which eye has not seen and ear has not heard, and [which] have not entered” into the heart of man, the things which God has prepared for them that love Him, as Moses and some of the saints have said.
28.22: As then we have hoped in Him, let us give to Him praise; and to Him be glory and might for ever and ever. Amen.
28.24: Cor. Ii. (almost exactly); not as in Isa. Lxiv.. The reference is perhaps to Deut. Xxix.; but it is more probably a blunder.
28.25: After the people are taught the Initiation’ into the mysteries, let the Eucharist be offered; but let not the Initiation into the mysteries be said each time, but only at Pascha, on Saturday, and on the first day of the week, and on the days of the Epiphany and of Pentecost.

29: OF WHAT SORT A PRESBYTER OUGHT TO BE
29.1: Let a presbyter be ordained being testified to by all the people, according to what has been said before; skilled in reading, meek, poor not money-loving, having laboured much in ministrations among the weak, proved to be pure, without blame; if he have been as a father to the orphans, if he have ministered to the poor; if he have not grown cold [in his love] for the Church’; if in all things he be pious, quiet, so that being [thus] he may in all respects be worthy to have those things that are fitting and suitable revealed to him by God, and also may be counted worthy of the gift of healing.

30.1: Then let the appointment of the presbyter be thus. All the priestly company conducting him, the bishop laying his hand on his head, the presbyters touching him and holding him, let the bishop begin, and say thus.
30: PRAYER OF ORDINATION OF A PRESBYTER
30.2: O God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Ineffable One, the Light, who have neither beginning nor ending,’ the Lord, who have ordered‘ all things, and set bounds to [them ], and by reason have defined the order of all things by You created; Hear us, and look upon this Your servant, and make him partaker of, and grant to him, the Spirit of grace and of reason and of strength, the Spirit of the presbyterate who does not grow old,’ and is indissoluble, homogeneous loving the faithful, rebuking, that he may help and govern Your people by labour, by fear, by a pure heart, by holiness, by excellency, by wisdom, and by the working of the Holy Spirit, through Your care, O Lord.
30.3: In like manner as when you did look upon Your People, the Chosen, you did command Moses to ask for the elders and filling [them] with Your Spirit bestowed Him on Your minister! So now, O Lord, bestow on [this man] abundantly Your Spirit, whom you did give to those who by Yourself were made disciples, and to all those who through them truly believed in You And make him worthy, being filled with Your wisdom and Your hidden mysteries, to feed Your people in holiness of heart: pure, and true; praising, blessing, lauding, giving thanks, offering a doxology alway, day and night, to Your holy and glorious Name; labouring with cheerfulness and patience to be a vessel of Your Holy Spirit; having and bearing alway the cross of Your Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom [be] praise and might to You with the Holy Spirit for ever and ever.
30.5: Let both the priests and people give him the Peace, with a holy kiss.

31.1: After he is [ordained] let him be constant at the altar, making prayers laboriously without ceasing. But sometimes alone in some house let him take a rest from the things which belong to the house of the Lord; but not ceasing, or diminishing [one] hour, from prayers.
31.2: Let him fast three days each [week ] all the year, [on the] one [hand] that he may be perfected in intelligence; and moreover [let him fast] according to his strength, not wandering about and going here and there with every spirit, but doing everything with energy.
31.3: If it is revealed to a presbyter or bishop to speak, let him speak; but if not, let him not neglect and despise his work,
31.4: If it be revealed to a presbyter to visit his parishes and speak the word, let him go; but if not, let him entreat God with supplication; and if it is revealed to him to speak to them, let him speak to them, always taking the burden and load of Him who was crucified for him, and praying for all the people.
31.5: Let not a presbyter or bishop be anxious about food or clothing. God takes thought and cares for His own in the [things ] which He knows.
31.6: But if, when he receives from any one food or clothing,’ it be said to him that he should receive also from another, let it suffice him to receive from [the first] alone, and that [only] in so far as is fitting, and as he needs, and not to excess.
31.7: In respect of firmness of faith, let a presbyter always be unchangeable; for it is such as these that God desires.
31.8: And let him prove the heart of each one; lest evil kept and buried within, make him a stranger to the grace of God.
31.9: Let him not neglect nor despise those who do good works through teaching! But let him watch for signs in them; [and] of those [signs appearing] in them let him judge spiritually by [their] sighs, weeping, earnest conversations, silence, sadness, patience, humble bowing of the head.? But that which best trains and causes suffering is weeping and groaning.
31.10: But the work [these do] is watching, continence, fasting, quietness, unceasing prayer, meditation, faith, meekness, philanthropy, labour, weariness, love, subjection, goodness, gravity, and every [work of] light.
31.11: [On the other hand], the signs of those who do not bring forth the fruits of life are [these]:—-sloth, love of pleasure, eyes wandering in all directions, disobedience, complaining, restlessness, a laziness’ that will not move,’ wandering about.
31.12: But the work [these do] is gluttony, debauchery, anger, unbelief, idle and unseasonable laughter, confusion, neglect, error, disturbance, wantonness, love of gains, love of money, envy, contention, drunkenness, high-mindedness, vain talking, love of praise, and every [work of] darkness.
31.13: Let him recognise products such as these, and let him speak to those who are worthy. But let him not waste time! Upon those who do not receive [his teaching]. For those who sow on earth without fruits shall reap miseries.
31.14: Let the presbyter, as is right and fitting, go about to the houses of those who are sick with the deacon, and visit them; let him consider and say to them those things that are fitting and proper, especially to the faithful. Let him exhort that the sick who are poor be helped by the Church, so that they also who do [deeds] of kindness may enter into the joy
31.15: Of their Lord Let him confirm those who have newly become catechumens with prophetical and evangelical utterances, with the word of teaching. Let him not neglect his prayers, for he is the figure of the archangels: but let him know that God did not spare the angels who sinned.
31.16: Let him fast; and if it is proper, let him receive of the cup. Let wine suffice him, as much as, in his judgment, profits and helps him, lest that drink which was for [his] healing he receive to [his] loss In sickness, let him eat herbs and fish, and also that he may have care for his work. In everything let the priest be an example to the faithful of the work of holiness.’
31.17: Let the presbyter praise and give thanks in the same way as the bishop.

32.1: Let them say the daily hymn of praise in the Church, each of them at his own time, thus.
32.2: The grace of our Lord [be] with you all.
32.3: The people: And with your spirit.
32.4: The priest: Praise you the Lord.
32.5: The people: It is fitting and right.
32.6: The priest: You, O Father of incorruptibility, Deliverer of our souls, Confirmer of the thoughts, and Guardian of our hearts, who have illumined our hearts and have brought to an end the darkness of our intelligence, by the knowledge which is in You; who have by the cross of Your Only - begotten brought back anew to incorruptibility the old man which was given over to corruption; who have brought error to an end, and by Your commandments have made man‘ to pass to immortality; who sought that which was lost, we [Your] servants [and] also [Your] people praise.
32.7: The people: We praise You, and the rest.
32.8: The priest: We praise You, O Lord, whom continually the unceasing doxologies of the Archangels singing praise, and the hymns of praise of Glories and chants of Dominions praise.
32.9: We praise You, O Lord, who sent Your Thought, Your Word, Your Wisdom, Your Energy,’ [namely] Him who [is] of old, and was with You before the worlds, the uncreated Word of the Uncreated one, but appeared, incarnate, in the end of times, for the salvation of created man, Your beloved Son Jesus Christ, who made us free from the yoke of slavery.
32.10: Therefore we also, as we are accustomed, [we] Your servants, O Lord [and] also [your] people, praise You.
32.11: The people: We praise You, and the rest.
32.12: The priest: We sing to You a triple hymn of praise from our hearts, O Lord who give life, to You who visit the souls of the poor, and neglect not the spirits of those who are afflicted, the Assister of those who are persecuted, the Helper of those who are tossed on the sea, the Deliverer of those who are buffeted, the Provider for those who are hungry, who take vengeance for those who are wronged, the Lover of the faithful, the Companion of the saints, the Habitation of the pure, the Dwelling-place of those who call on You in truth, the Protector of widows, the Liberator of orphans, who give to Your Church a right government, and have founded in it love-feasts, ministrations, receptions’ of the faithful, the partaking of the Spirit, gifts of grace and powers.
32.13: We praise You; we cease not alway in our hearts picturing the image of Your kingdom in ourselves, for Your sake [and] also [for the sake] of Your beloved Son Jesus Christ, by whom [be] praise and might to You with the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever, Amen.
32.14: And let the people say: Amen.
32.15: But if also any one says prophetical words, let him say [them]; he has a reward.
32.16: But at midnight let the sons of priestly service, and those of the people who are more perfect, give praise by themselves. For also in that hour our Lord, rising, praised His Father.
32.17: Of the Lord, walks as He walked in this world, that where He is, there he may be also.

33.1: The deacon is appointed, chosen like the things which have before been spoken of. If he is of good conduct,’ if he is pure, if he have been chosen for purity and for abstinence from distractions; if not, yet [if he] be the husband of one wife,’ borne witness to by all the faithful, not entangled in the businesses of the world, not knowing a handicraft, without riches, without children.
33.2: But if he is married or! Have children, let his children be taught to work piety and to be pure, so that they may be approved by the Church,’ according to the rule of the ministry. But let the Church take care for them, so that they may persevere in the law and in the work of the ministry.

34.1: But let him accomplish in the Church those things which are right. Let [his] ministry be thus.
34.2: First, let him do only those things which are commanded by the bishop as for proclamation!; and let him be the counsellor of the whole clergy and the mystery of the Church; who ministers to the sick, who ministers to the strangers, who helps the widows, who is the father of the orphans, who goes about all the houses of those that are in need, lest any be in affliction or sickness or misery.
34.3: Let him go about in the houses of the catechumens, so that he may confirm those who are doubting and teach those who are unlearned.
34.4: Let him clothe those men who have departed,’ adorning [them]; burying’ the strangers; guiding those who pass from their dwelling, or go into captivity. For the help of those who are in need let him notify the Church; let him not trouble the bishop; but only on the first day of the week let him make mention about everything, so that he may know.
34.5: Let him be watchful at the hour of the assembly, going about in the church, and let him see that no one be [ there who is] proud, or a buffoon, or a spy,’ or one who speaks idle [words]. Let him rebuke [such], every one seeing and hearing, and let him thrust out him whom he has condemned to receive punishment, so that the others also may fear.
34.6: And if [the offender] persuade him to permit him to partake, let him give him comfort.
34.7: But if the man persist in his transgression or disorderliness, let him take [word] about him up to the bishop, and let him be separated seven days, and then called; so that he is not taken captive.” But if when he comes he still continue and persist in his folly, let him be cut off until he, repenting truly, come to himself, begging [to be received back,
34.8: If he is in a city on the seashore, let him go quickly about the places on the seashore, lest there is any one dead in the sea; let him clothe him and bury him.
34.9: Similarly also let him search out the guest house,’ lest there is any one who is staying in the place sick or in need or dead; and let him make [it] known to the Church, so that it may provide what is right for each one. Let him cause the palsied and infirm to bathe‘ as is right, so that they may have a breathing space from their pains.
34.10: Let him give through the Church to each one what is right.
34.11: In the Church let twelve presbyters, seven deacons, fourteen subdeacons, thirteen widows who sit in front,’ be known.
34.12: But of the deacons let him who is considered among them to be most earnest, and best in governing, be chosen to be the receiver of strangers. Let him alway be in the place of the guest house which is in the church, clothed in white garments, a stole only on his shoulder.

35.1: Let him be in everything as the eye of the Church, with fear admonishing, so that he may be an example to! The people of piety Let him admonish thus.
35.3: Let every one know his place.
35.5: [Lift] up the eyes of your hearts.
35.8: Let no sexually immoral person, no wrathful man? [remain]; if one who is a servant of evil be [here], let him withdraw.
35.9: Our Lord and our God and our Savior Jesus Christ.
35.10: When the presbyter or bishop begins the prayer, let the people pray and kneel.
35.11: Then let the deacon say thus.
35.12: For the peace which is from heaven let us beg, that the Lord in His mercy may give us peace.
35.13: For our faith let us beg, that the Lord may grant to us to keep truly to the end the faith which is in Him.
35.14: For harmony and concord let us beg, that the Lord may keep us together in concord of the Spirit.
35.15: For patience let us beg, that the Lord may bestow [upon us patience to the end in all afflictions.
35.16: For the Apostles let us beg, that the Lord may grant to us to please Him, as they also pleased Him, and may make us worthy of their inheritance.
35.17: For the holy prophets let us beg, that the Lord may number us with them.
35.18: For the holy confessors let us beg, that the Lord God may grant us to fulfill [our course] with the same mind [as they].
35.19: For the bishop let us beg, that our Lord may grant him to us for length of days’ in faith, rightly dividing the word of truth, and standing at the head of the Church purely and without blame.
35.20: For the presbyterate let us beg, that the Lord may not take away from them the spirit of the presbyterate, but bestow on them earnestness and piety until the end.
35.21: For the deacons let us beg, that the Lord may grant to them to run a perfect course, and to perfect holiness, and that He may remember their work and their love.
35.22: For the presbyteresses let us beg, that the Lord may hear their supplications and keep their hearts perfectly in the grace of the Spirit and help their work.
35.23: For the subdeacons, readers, deaconesses let us beg, that the Lord may grant to them to receive a reward in patience.
35.24: For the faithful laymen let us beg, that the Lord may grant to them to keep the faith perfectly.
35.25: For the catechumens let us beg, that the Lord may grant to them to be counted worthy of the laver of forgiveness, and may sanctify them with the seal of holiness.
35.26: For the kingdom let us beg, that the Lord may bestow upon it tranquillity.
35.27: For the exalted powers let us beg, that the Lord may grant to them prudence and the fear of Him.
35.28: For all the world let us beg, that the Lord may provide for each one such things as are fitting.
35.29: For those who travel by sea, and those who go on journeys let us beg, that the Lord may guide them with the right hand of mercy.
35.30: For those who are persecuted let us beg, that the Lord may grant to them patience and knowledge, and may bestow on them also a completed labour.
35.31: For those who have fallen asleep from the Church let us beg, that the Lord may bestow upon them a place of rest.
35.32: For those who have fallen let us beg, that the Lord may not remember their follies to them, but moderate [His] threats to them.
35.33: And let us all also, who need prayer, beg that the Lord may protect and keep us with the peaceful Spirit.
35.34: Let us persuade and beg the Lord, that He may receive our prayers.
35.35: After the deacon commemorates, let the bishop make a sign with his hand.
35.36: Let the deacon say: Let us arise in the Holy Spirit, that, being made wise, we may grow in His grace, boasting in His Name; being built on the foundation of the Apostles,’ let us beg [and] beg the Lord that, being persuaded, He may receive our prayers.
35.37: Then let the bishop complete [the prayer]. And let the people say: Amen.

36.1: Let the deacon be such as this, so that he may appear with fear and modesty and reverence. With regard to fervour of spirit, let him have a perfect manner of life. Let him observe and look at those who come into the house of the sanctuary. Let him investigate who they are, so that he may know if they are lambs or wolves.
36.2: And when he asks, let him bring in him that is worthy, lest, if a spy enter, the liberty of the Church be searched out, and his sin be on his head.
36.3: If any one come late to the [service of] praise, either when that of the dawn is being said or when the Offering is being offered, whoever he be, let him remain outside, and let not the deacon bring him in,—for it’ is a type of the day of judgment which is to come,—lest by the noise of the entrance there is distraction to those who are praying.
36.4: But when he comes and finds that the door is shut,’ let him not knock, because of what has been said already.
36.5: But after the hymn of praise which is placed first is finished, let the faithful man or faithful woman enter. Let the deacon say, either, Over the offering: or, For! The hymn of praise, let us beg that the Lord may write our supplication! In the book of life, and [that] God who [is] for ever may remember us in His holy habitations of light. For?
36.6: [this] brother who is late, let us beg that the Lord may give him earnestness and labour, and turn away from him every bond of this world, and give him the will of affection and love and hope.
36.7: Similarly also for a sister or for a deaconess, for those who are’ late or remain outside, let him admonish that all the people may beg for them. For thus when a deacon mentions and admonishes about them, earnestness is strengthened and the bond of love ‘" is fulfilled, and the despiser and the slothful is disciplined.

37.1: If” any woman whatsoever suffer violence from a man, let the deacon accurately investigate if she is faithful’ and have truly suffered violence; if! He who treated her with violence was not her lover.
37.2: And if she is accurately thus, and if she that suffered mourn about the violence that happened to her, let him take it up to the hearing of the bishop, that she may be shewn to be in all things in communion with’ the Church. If he who treated her with violence be faithful, let not the deacon bring him into the church for partaking,” even if he repent.
37.3: But if he is a catechumen and repent, let him be baptized and partake. Let the deacon catechise those who repent and bring them to the presbyters or to the bishop that they may be catechised and taught knowledge.
37.4: But if [his] power suffice to accom- plish perfectly the office of the diaconate, let him abide only in prayer; and let him consider supplication and meditation, love, the! Way, mourning, and [to have] fear before his eyes, as a work; and he shall be called a son of the light.

38.1: Let the appointment of a deacon be thus. Let the bishop alone lay a hand on him, because he is not appointed to the priesthood, but for the service of attendance on the bishop and the Church.? Over the deacon then, let the bishop say thus.
38: PRAYER OF ORDINATION OF A DEACON
38.2: O God, who created all things, and adorned [them] by the Word; who rest in the pure ages; who ministered to us eternal life by Your prophets; who enlightened us with the light of knowledge; O God, who do great things,’ and [are] the Maker of all glory’ Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, whom you did send to minister to Your will, that all the race of mankind might be saved, and made known to us and revealed Your Thought, Your Wisdom, Your Energy, Your beloved Son, Jesus Christ, the Lord of light, the Prince of princes, and God of gods; give the spirit of grace and earnestness to" this Your servant, that there may be given to him earnestness, quiet, strength, power to please You; give him, O Lord, as a worker in the law without shame, kind, a lover of orphans, a lover of the pious, a lover of widows, fervent in spirit, a lover of good things; and enlighten, O Lord, him whom You have loved and chosen to minister to Your Church, offering in holiness to Your holy place those things which are offered to You from the inheritance of Your high priesthood; so that ministering without blame and purely and holily and with a pure conscience, he may be counted worthy of this high and exalted office, by Your good will, praising You continually through Your Only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, our Lord, by whom [be] praise and might to You for ever and ever.

39.1: If [one] be borne witness to and confess that he was in bonds and in imprisonment and in afflictions for the Name of God, a hand is not therefore laid on him for the diaconate. Similarly not for the presbyterate. For he has the honor of the clergy,’ having been protected by the hand of God, by [his] confessorship.
39.2: But if he is appointed bishop, he is also counted worthy of laying on of the hand. And [even] if he is a confessor who has not been judged before the power, and has not been buffeted in bonds, but only has confessed, he is counted worthy of laying on of the hand. For he receives the prayer of the clergy.
39.3: But let him not pray over him repeating” all these words; but when the shepherd advances he will receive the effect.

40.1: Let a widow be appointed, being chosen, if for a long time past she have abided without a husband; if though often

41.1: Let the appointment! Be thus. As she prays at the entrance of the altar and looks down, let the bishop say quietly, so that the priests may hear, thus.
41: PRAYER OF THE INSTITUTION? OF WIDOWS WHO SIT IN FRONT
41.2: O God, the Holy One, the Most High, who see the [things] that are humble, who have chosen the weak and the mighty; the Honoured One who have created also those [things] which are despised; give, O Lord, the spirit of power to this Your handmaid, and strengthen her with Your truth, so that doing Your commandment and serving in the house of Your sanctuary, she may be an honoured vessel to You, and may glorify!?
41.3: [You] in the day when You will glorify Your poor, O Lord. And grant to her power cheerfully to accomplish Your teachings which You have determined for a rule for Your handmaid. Grant to her, O Lord, the spirit of meekness and of power and of patience and of kindness, so that, bearing with ineffable joy Your burden, she may endure labours.
41.4: Yes, O Lord God, who know our weakness, perfect Your handmaid for the praise of Your house; strengthen her for edification and a good example,’ sanctify [her], make [her] wise; comfort [her] O God; for blessed and glorious” is Your kingdom, O God the Father.
41.5: And to You [be] praise, and to Your Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the Holy Spirit [who is] good and adorable and the Maker of life,” and of equal essence with You,” now and before all the worlds and for the ages and for ever and ever. The people: Amen.

42.1: My sanctuaries;! They shall shine in My glory in the day of recompense.

43.1: [Let her hymns of praise be said thus quietly:]
43: NIGHT HYMN OF PRAISE OF WIDOWS
HYMNS OF PRAISE AT DAWN OF WIDOWS WHO SIT IN FRONT
43.2: Holy, holy, without spot, who have Your dwelling in the light, God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, God of Enoch and David, of Elijah, of Elisha, of Moses, of Joshua, and of the prophets and of the others who in truth preached Your Name, God of the Apostles, the God who have guided all things by Your reason and have blessed them who lovingly trust in You; my soul praises You with the power of the spirit of my power, my heart praises You, O Lord, and Your might, alway.
43.3: Let all my power praise You, O Lord, for if You will, J am Yours, O God, the God of the poor; for You are the Helper of them that lack, and You are He that looks on the meek, and the Assister of the weak; assist me, O Lord, because by Your grace You were well pleased in me that I should be Your handmaid, for You have bestowed upon me a great name, that I should be called a Christian.
43.4: You who have freed me from servitude that I may serve a servitude to God, the Mighty One who [are] for ever, who see all, that I may praise You uncondemned. Yes, O Lord God, confirm my heart in You until it is perfected in the Holy Spirit.
43.5: Rejuvenate us for the edification of Your holy Church, Son and Word and Thought of the Father, the Christ who came for the salvation of the race of man, who suffered and were buried, and rose, [and] also were glorified by Him who sent You, turn, help, O Lord, set upright our thoughts by the strong faith of the Spirit. Glorify Your Name in us.
43.6: For in Your Father and in You and in the Holy Spirit is our hope for ever and ever.
43.7: With those who are with her let her say: Amen. But let her say the hymn of praise at dawn thus.
43.8: O Eternal God, Guide of our souls, Maker of light, Treasure of life, who rest! In the praises and prayers of the holy ones, Lover of compassion merciful, kind, King of all, and God, our Lord, my spirit praises [You], sending [up] to You the unceasing voices of Your handmaid, O Lord, who beseeches You that You may perfect in Your handmaid the spirit of reason and of piety and of right knowledge.
43.9: I praise You, O Lord, who took away from our poverty all disturbance and confusion, wrath and all contention and evil habit, who prepared [and] changed the feelings of my understanding that I might serve You only, O God; who have adorned Your holy Church with various ministries, who drive away from Your handmaid all doubtfulness, fear, weakness; and hold the thoughts of those who rightly serve You; I praise You, O God, who have enlightened me with the light of Your knowledge, through Your Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom [be] praise and might to You for ever and ever.
43.11: And with those who are with her let her say: Amen.

44.1: Similarly let a subdeacon be appointed who is chaste, the bishop praying over him. Let the bishop say over him on the first day of the week, in the hearing of all the people, thus.
44.2: You, O N., minister and hear the Gospel in the fear of God. Cultivate holily the knowledge of your soul; keep pureness; discipline yourself; observe and obey and hear meekly; neglect not prayers and fasts, so that the Lord may give you rest and make you worthy of a higher degree.
44.3: And let all the priests say: So be it, so be it, so be it.

45.1: A reader is instituted [who is pure, quiet, meek,’ wise, with much experience, learned and of much learning, with a good memory, vigilant, so that he may deserve a higher degree? First let the book be given him in the sight of the people, on the first day of the week. But a hand is not laid on him. But he hears from the bishop [the following].
45.2: You, O N., whom Christ has called to be a minister’ of His words, be careful, and strive that you may appear approved both in this rule and in a higher degree, even by our Lord Jesus Christ; so that He in His everlasting habitations may pay you a good reward for these things.
45.3: And let the priests say: So be it, so be it, so be it.

46.1: A male or female virgin is not instituted" or appointed by man,” but is voluntarily separated and named [a virgin].
46.2: But a hand is not laid on him, as for virginity. For this division! Is of [their] own free will. But it is right for virgins that they be fixed and bound in the suffering of a sound body, that they be constant in fasts and in prayers, in weeping and in mourning daily; but that they alway expect a departure from the flesh, and strive as at the departure.
46.3: Let them not serve raging or debauchery or drunkenness or vain talking, or [be engaged] in worldly work or in distraction,’ but they are as one who is on’ the cross; let their hearts be [lifted] up, with all meekness of thought and comeliness, with meditation on the Holy Scriptures, with faithful thoughts’ with kind consolations, so that when they pray they may be answered concerning those things which they ask for the faithful who wish to provide for them.
46.4: Let them not despise [these things], so that through them also a portion of life may be divided to those Let them be confirmed in love and kindness and in true and perfect grace. Let them be constant in consolation, consoling their neighbors, catechising and teaching those who have lately been made faithful, in understanding and in knowledge and in kindness, inciting those who are very young, being examples of holiness among them in all good things.
46.5: Similarly also let the females do. But in order and in grace and in knowledge let them speak and work,” that they may truly be the salt of the earth! As it is called.
46.6: But” let females who are virgins have their heads covered in the church, and let them hide only their hair; but let them be counted worthy of honor from every one, in order that the rest [of the women] who desire, may emulate them.

47.1: If any one appear in the people to have a gift of healing or of knowledge or of tongues, a hand is not laid on him, for the work is manifest. But let them have honor.
